clue.text: Busy work mounting bugs famed oil worker

indicators.note: in a down clue, mounting means climbing upwards, so the word for work is read from bottom to top

parts.note: OP is short for opus, a musical work; it climbs, so it will read backwards
lice are small bugs
John Constable, the English landscape painter who worked in oils

explanation.surface: A busy job on an oil rig, with a famous worker bothered by insects.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Busy' is not an adjective here: it is old British slang for a police officer, especially a detective. The 'oil worker' is an artist working in oil paint, not a rig hand.
explanation.definitionFit: British criminal slang calls a policeman a busy, from the idea of officers always poking around in other people's business.

clue.text: Aura surrounding old tribe in Moroccan location

indicators.note: surrounding says the word for aura wraps itself around the ancient tribe

parts.note: an aura is an air or atmosphere about someone
Gad was one of the twelve tribes of Israel

explanation.surface: Someone with a mystical aura hanging around an ancient tribe somewhere in Morocco.
explanation.walkthrough: The tribe is one of the twelve tribes of Israel, a crossword regular; the aura word opens after its first letter to take it in.
explanation.definitionFit: Agadir is a large port city and beach resort on the Atlantic coast of southern Morocco.

clue.text: Lark circling sailor caught — a bleak prospect?

indicators.note: circling says the word for lark goes right round the sailor and the catch

parts.note: a lark or antic is a playful prank
tar is the old word for a seaman
c is the cricket scorecard abbreviation for caught
kept as it stands

explanation.surface: A cheerful escapade goes wrong when a sailor is caught, leaving a grim outlook.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags that 'bleak prospect' is a view or landscape, not a gloomy future; the lark word splits after two letters to hold the sailor and the catch.
explanation.definitionFit: The frozen southern continent is a literally bleak landscape to look out over, ice and wind with barely any life.

clue.text: Gypsy turning up with beer and spirits

indicators.note: in a down clue, turning up flips the word so it reads bottom to top

parts.note: a Rom is a member of the Romani people; turning up, it will read backwards
ale is beer, and 'with' adds it

explanation.surface: A traveller arrives with beer and spirits, ready for a party.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Spirits' looks like more drink to go with the beer, but it means mood. ROM is a Romani person.
explanation.definitionFit: Morale is the confidence and mood of a person or group, which is what we mean by keeping someone's spirits up.

clue.text: Large adhesive label covers disciplinarian

indicators.note: a label that covers something takes it inside, so the label's letters go around the large abbreviation

parts.note: a sticker is a label with glue on the back
L is the clothing-size abbreviation for large

explanation.surface: A big sticky label is slapped over a strict schoolteacher.
explanation.walkthrough: STICKER opens between K and E to take in L.
explanation.definitionFit: A stickler insists on rules being followed to the letter, as a strict enforcer of discipline would.

clue.text: Here camels roaming spit on one

parts.note: British slang for spittle, or to spit
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: Wandering camels are notorious for spitting on anyone nearby.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface feeds you camels and spitting, and the spit is part of the wordplay. To gob is British slang for to spit; 'on' puts GOB before I.
explanation.definitionFit: The Gobi is the great desert of Mongolia and northern China, home to wild Bactrian camels wandering its plains.

clue.text: Material about eastern Mediterranean region

parts.note: re means about or concerning
the Levant is the old name for the lands at the eastern end of the Mediterranean

explanation.surface: Some fabric or cloth concerning an area of the eastern Mediterranean.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Material' reads as a noun, cloth, but is the adjective, as in 'material evidence'.
explanation.definitionFit: In legal and formal usage, material evidence is pertinent evidence, bearing directly on the matter being decided.

clue.text: Reproduction Stonehenge assembled in capital

indicators.note: in places the rearranged monument inside the French capital city

parts.note: Paris is the capital of France

indicators.note: the ancient stones are assembled afresh, put together in a new arrangement

parts.note: anagram fodder, 10 letters

explanation.surface: A replica of Stonehenge has been built in a capital city.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Reproduction' tempts as a replica, which the surface supports, but it is biological reproduction; the French capital splits after three letters to hold the rearranged stones.
explanation.definitionFit: Parthenogenesis is a form of reproduction without fertilisation, where an egg develops without a male, as in aphids and some lizards.

clue.text: See two newspapers coming round for church feature

indicators.note: the two papers come round, so they sit on either side of the word for see

parts.note: an organ is a newspaper or journal speaking for a group
lo is the old word for look or see
FT is the Financial Times

explanation.surface: Someone checks two papers delivered to them in search of a story about a church.
explanation.walkthrough: One fragment serves both papers: a party organ and the FT, the Financial Times, go either side of LO.
explanation.definitionFit: The raised gallery that holds a church's pipes and keyboards is a standard piece of church architecture.

clue.text: Longer and shorter periods reversed in final letter

indicators.note: the two time spans together are written backwards

parts.note: an age is a long period of time
a mo is a moment, a very short time

explanation.surface: Someone is swapping around long and short time spans in the last letter of a document.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Periods' serves both halves: a longer one, AGE, and a shorter one, MO. AGEMO read backwards gives the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Omega is the last of the twenty-four characters of the Greek alphabet, hence also a byword for the end.

clue.text: Excellent daughters returned to home land

parts.note: at home is in

indicators.note: the excellent and daughters pair is returned, sent back the way it came

parts.note: A1 means first-rate, with the 1 read as I
d is the genealogical abbreviation for daughter

explanation.surface: Fine young women came back home to their native country.
explanation.walkthrough: A1, read with the digit as the letter I, gives AI; with D it reverses to DIA, which is attached to IN.
explanation.definitionFit: India is a country, and 'land' is the everyday poetic synonym for nation or country.

clue.text: Designer makes Catholic dose with ecstasy during play

indicators.note: during a play means inside it, so the Catholic, dose and ecstasy go inside the play

parts.note: to act is to play a part
RC is Roman Catholic
a hit is a dose of a drug
E is slang for the drug ecstasy

explanation.surface: A fashion designer's play has a Catholic character taking ecstasy mid-scene.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Designer' suggests fashion; here it is of buildings. 'Dose' is drug slang, a single hit, and E is ecstasy.
explanation.definitionFit: An architect is the professional who plans and draws up buildings, the person who designs them.

clue.text: Artist seen in every echo? Listener's smart!

indicators.note: the artist is seen inside the word for every

parts.note: each and every
RA is a Royal Academician
Echo is the NATO alphabet word for E

explanation.surface: An artist hears echoes everywhere, and his listener remarks how clever it all is.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Smart' looks like clever, but it is a noun: a sting or pain. The listener is the ear. The artist is a Royal Academician.
explanation.definitionFit: To smart is to sting with pain, and an ear, the organ that listens, suffering that pain has an earache.

clue.text: Recline to consume honeyed drink and quencher

indicators.note: to consume is to swallow, so the word for recline takes the honeyed drink inside

parts.note: to recline is to lie down
mead is the alcoholic drink made from honey

explanation.surface: Lounging back while sipping a honey drink to quench one's thirst.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Quencher' alone is the definition, short for thirst-quencher; 'and' just joins it to the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: Limeade is a sweetened lime-flavoured soft drink, the kind of cold beverage taken to satisfy thirst.

clue.text: Tees upset about hypocrisy concerning trade

parts.note: the setter, Tees, refers to himself as me

indicators.note: about means around, so the word for upset goes around the hypocrisy

parts.note: to rile is to upset or anger
cant is insincere, hypocritical talk

explanation.surface: The setter is angry about hypocrisy in business dealings.
explanation.walkthrough: The setter signs this puzzle Tees, so 'Tees' means me. 'Upset' looks like an anagram signal but is a plain verb, which opens after its first letter to hold the hypocrisy.
explanation.definitionFit: Mercantile means relating to merchants and commerce, as in mercantile law or the mercantile marine.

clue.text: Fine beer to be sent round for beast

parts.note: OK means fine

indicators.note: the beer is sent round, turned to face the other way

parts.note: IPA is India pale ale

explanation.surface: Good beer sent round a pub for an animal to drink.
explanation.walkthrough: IPA, India pale ale, is a common beer abbreviation; turned round it follows OK.
explanation.definitionFit: The okapi is a forest mammal of central Africa, a giraffe relative with striped legs, so an animal.

clue.text: Notice six-footer eating cake that's rich

indicators.note: eating takes the cake inside, into the notice-and-insect pair

parts.note: an ad is a notice or advertisement
a bun is a small cake
an insect has six feet, and an ant is an insect

explanation.surface: Look at that very tall person eating a rich cake.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Six-footer' suggests a tall person, but it is an insect, with six feet. 'Rich' is the definition, not a description of the cake.
explanation.definitionFit: Rich in the sense of plentiful or copious, as in rich in natural resources, is a synonym here.

clue.text: See 20
Deeply impressed after heartless 18 Across, but miserable

indicators.note: after places the deeply impressed word behind the remains of 18 Across
heartless takes away the middle of 18 Across, keeping only its outside

parts.note: 18 Across is the conflict word, with its middle letter gone
etched means cut deep into a surface, as an image is impressed

explanation.surface: Someone deeply moved by a war, but unhappy nonetheless.
explanation.walkthrough: 18 Across is WAR, the second word of 20 Across; removing the central A leaves WR.
explanation.definitionFit: Wretched means in a very unhappy or unfortunate state, a direct synonym of miserable.

clue.text: Correlation shown where moon follows rodent

indicators.note: follows puts the moon behind the rodent in reading order

parts.note: a rat is a rodent
Io is one of the moons of Jupiter

explanation.surface: A statistician notes a pattern where a moon trails a rat across the sky.
explanation.walkthrough: IO, a moon of Jupiter, is a crossword favourite.
explanation.definitionFit: A ratio expresses the relationship between two quantities, a numerical correspondence between them.

clue.text: It needs treatment, rough, for backing protocol row

parts.note: it is sex appeal, SA
usage is the way something is treated or handled

indicators.note: backing means moving backwards, so the word for rough is read in reverse

parts.note: raw means rough or unrefined
surface padding: it simply sets the next piece beside the first

explanation.surface: Something in a bad way needs rough treatment to support its official procedures.
explanation.walkthrough: 'It' for sex appeal is an old convention; 'needs' just places USAGE beside SA. The Northern Ireland Protocol, part of the Brexit deal, led to a 2021 UK-EU dispute over chilled meats entering Northern Ireland.
explanation.definitionFit: The 2021 argument over British chilled meats under the Northern Ireland Protocol was nicknamed by the press after the banger itself.

clue.text: By it one develops feeling for character

definitions.text: By it one develops feeling for character

parts.words: By it one develops feeling for character
parts.note: surface reading: some experience that helps a person grow in empathy and understand others' personalities
setter's reading: touching printed letters with the fingertips, a character being a letter

explanation.walkthrough: 'Character' reads as personality and 'feeling' as emotion; in fact a character is a letter and feeling is touch, so this is the raised-dot reading system for blind people.
explanation.definitionFit: The raised-dot writing system lets blind readers identify letters by running fingertips over the page.

clue.text: Split in religious group that goes both ways?

parts.note: bi is slang for bisexual, someone who swings both ways
a sect is a religious group

explanation.surface: A schism opens in a religious community that is pulling in two directions.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Goes both ways' is informal for bisexual; its short form comes first in the answer although the clue lists it second.
explanation.definitionFit: To bisect is to cut into two equal parts, which is splitting something down the middle.

clue.text: Reprieves ram trapped among the French

indicators.note: the ram is trapped among the French article, held inside it

parts.note: les is the plural 'the' in French
a tup is a ram, a male sheep

explanation.surface: A ram caught among French people is spared the chop.
explanation.walkthrough: Tup is a northern British farming word for a ram; the French plural article wraps around it.
explanation.definitionFit: A let-up is a pause or easing of pressure, a respite, which is what a reprieve gives.

clue.text: Hearings in case due to be rescheduled

indicators.note: rescheduled things are put in a new order, as these letters are

parts.note: anagram fodder, 9 letters

explanation.surface: Court hearings in a case that is due to be moved to another date.
explanation.walkthrough: The legal surface makes 'Hearings' look like court sessions, and that is fair: formal hearings are also this word.
explanation.definitionFit: An audience can be a formal interview or hearing, as when someone is granted an audience with the Pope.

clue.text: Poet's black book one that's devious keeps

indicators.note: to keep is to hold, so the scrambled one holds the book
devious means off the straight path, so the letters of one wander

parts.note: anagram fodder
b is the abbreviation for book

explanation.surface: A poet keeps a little black book, and somebody sly is holding onto it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Poet's' marks a word found mainly in verse. 'Black book' sits together in the surface but splits: black is the definition, book the letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Ebon is a literary, poetic form of ebony, meaning deep dark in colour.

clue.text: Money short, then endlessly given in tax

indicators.note: short means cut off before the finish, so the money word loses its last letter
without an end, the word for then drops its final letter

parts.note: tin is slang for money, docked of its tail
then, docked of its tail

explanation.surface: Money is tight, and then all of it keeps being handed over in taxes.
explanation.walkthrough: TIN is old British slang for money.
explanation.definitionFit: A tithe was a tenth of produce or earnings paid to support the church, a traditional levy.

clue.text: Fish served with duck's tongue

parts.note: ling is a long cod-like sea fish
a duck is a score of nought in cricket, which looks like O

explanation.surface: A fish dish served alongside duck tongue on a menu.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket a duck is a score of zero, so O. 'Served with' simply sets O after LING, and 'duck's' is read as duck is.
explanation.definitionFit: Tongue means a language, and lingo is an informal, often jokey word for a language or jargon.

clue.text: Oil producers lie and cut pay anyway

indicators.note: anyway read as any way means the letters can go in any order

parts.note: anagram fodder
anagram fodder

explanation.surface: Oil companies lie and slash wages regardless.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Oil producers' reads as petroleum firms, but these are trees; 'anyway' breaks into any way.
explanation.definitionFit: Eucalyptus trees yield eucalyptus oil from their leaves, used in medicines and inhalants.
